snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹10–25 lakh for a clinic plus a team of home-visit therapists
snapshot.margin_production: Therapist pay is 40–60% of the fee once you run a team
snapshot.breakeven: 3–9 months on your own; 12–18 months for a team or clinic
snapshot.distribution_note: Orthopaedic doctors, hospitals and satisfied patients send most new patients

tailwinds: India's population is ageing, and more people need rehab after surgery or a stroke.
Desk jobs, gym injuries and sports have created steady demand for pain and posture treatment.
Hospitals discharge patients earlier, and families prefer rehab at home over daily hospital visits.
Physiotherapists are coming under formal registration through the 2021 allied-health law, which makes registered therapists easier to trust.
headwinds: You need a recognised physiotherapy degree (BPT or MPT); this isn't a business you can run without one.
Booking apps take a large share of the fee for each patient they send.
Travel between home visits limits how many patients one therapist can see.
Patients often stop coming as soon as the pain eases, before treatment is finished.
angle_2026: Home physiotherapy has become normal in Indian cities, helped by apps and hospitals that discharge patients sooner. In 2026 the independent therapists who do best have their own referral network of surgeons and hospitals and track patient progress in writing, which keeps patients coming until treatment is done.
cost_basis: Estimated for a qualified physiotherapist starting home visits, with a clinic as the scaled option, 2026 prices.

unit_economics.note: Five to six home visits a day is the practical ceiling for one therapist, so income grows through higher fees, clustered appointments or a team.

investor_probes: How many sessions does each therapist do per day, including travel?
What share of patients complete their full treatment plan?
How dependent are you on one hospital or one app for patients?
How do you check the quality of therapists you employ?
bootstrap_takeaway: Build relationships with three to five orthopaedic surgeons and a hospital discharge team, cluster your appointments by neighbourhood, and sell treatment packages instead of single sessions.
licences: A recognised BPT or MPT degree
Registration with your state physiotherapy council or allied-health council where it is in place
Shops and Establishments registration for a clinic
Healthcare services by qualified practitioners are generally exempt from GST; confirm your case with a CA

hard_truths.title: Travel caps your income
hard_truths.text: Every hour in traffic is an hour you can't bill. Group patients by area and time of day, and charge more for visits outside your core area.

hard_truths.title: Patients drop off early
hard_truths.text: Many patients stop once the pain eases, which hurts both their recovery and your income. Sell packages of sessions, set goals in writing and show progress.

hard_truths.title: Collecting payment
hard_truths.text: Collecting cash after each visit leads to missed payments. Take payment in advance for packages, and use UPI.

hard_truths.title: Growing beyond yourself
hard_truths.text: Once you hire other therapists, your reputation depends on their work. Standard protocols, patient feedback and regular reviews are needed before you add a second person.

plan_goal: The aim is ₹1 lakh a month in sessions and a steady stream of doctor referrals.

plan.title: Set up
steps: Check your registration status and buy indemnity insurance.
Buy portable equipment for the conditions you treat most.
Set your fees against clinics and apps in your area.

plan.title: Build referrals
steps: Meet 10 orthopaedic surgeons, GPs and hospital discharge teams.
Offer a free first assessment for referred patients.
Set up a Google Business profile and ask early patients for reviews.

plan.title: Fill your calendar
steps: Sell 10- and 20-session packages with written goals.
Run a free posture camp in an office or housing society.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Track sessions per day, completion rates and income per hour.
Drop areas that take too long to reach.
Decide whether to open a small clinic or hire a second therapist.
